response.title: Can I charge a power station from my truck and a roof solar panel at the same time without swapping cables at every stop?
response.answer:
Yes. You can charge a portable power station from your truck and a roof-mounted solar panel simultaneously, without swapping cables at every stop. The key is choosing the right charging setup.

There are two main ways to do this.

Option 1: Power station with dual charging inputs

This is the simplest setup, provided your power station supports simultaneous vehicle and solar charging.

Two independent inputs can charge one battery at the same time.

When driving, your truck and solar panel can both contribute power. When parked with the engine off, solar continues charging.

Important: Some power stations have separate physical connectors but share one internal charging controller. They may not support simultaneous inputs.

Option 2: DC-DC charger with solar MPPT

This is often the better solution for a permanent truck installation.

A dual-source charger manages both inputs and sends regulated power to a compatible power station.

This can provide automatic switching between alternator and solar charging, with no cable swapping.

However, the charger output must be compatible with your power station's charging input. Not every dual-source DC-DC charger can connect directly to a portable power station.

Which should you choose?

For either setup, use appropriate fusing, wire sizing, and engine-off isolation so the truck's starter battery isn't accidentally drained. Never combine raw solar and vehicle power with a simple Y-cable.

Two questions so I can recommend the exact setup

What power station do you have? (EcoFlow DELTA, Bluetti AC200, Jackery Explorer, Anker SOLIX, etc.)

What truck do you drive? (Year and model, such as 2023 Ford F-150.)

With those two details, I can tell you whether your station supports simultaneous charging, what equipment you need, and how to wire it so everything works automatically.
